newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Strangles traded in BSkyB.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Strangles traded in BSkyB.

text.p: A stock market plunge on Tuesday made for a lively session in the UK stock options market, with several active stock options, dealers said.
Satellite television broadcaster British Sky Broadcasting was busy in mixed trading and several volatility deals were struck in the September options series.

The biggest was a crossed trade in which 1,000 September 600 puts were traded at 24p, along with 1,000 September 650 calls at 33p in a strangle strategy. The buyer would expect BSkyB shares to be volatile enough that by expiry, they either fall below 543p or rise above 707p, when the deal makes money.

In contrast, the seller of the strangles expects the shares to be fairly flat and if they are anywhere between 600p-650p at expiry the options will be worthless and a maximum profit of 57p can be then be made.
At the close of business on the stock market, BSkyB shares were down 21-1/2p to 566-1/2p.

Over in Lloyds TSB Group,the main trade was a short straddle established by selling 500 September 650 puts and calls at 50p and 30-1/2p respectively, which will make a maximum profit of 80-1/2p if held to expiry.
Shares in the bank closed down 21p to 605-1/2p.
Elsewhere, in FTSE 100 index options one large deal was from a buyer of 2,000 September 4525 calls at 313p against selling 2,000 July 4900 calls at about 35p in a diagonal bear spread.
The deal may have been struck in order to own the September calls cheaply on expectations the market will go up between July and September expiry.
In contrast, another large deal was to buy 2,300 September 4250 puts at prices around 20-1/2p.
The FTSE index closed down 62.9 at 4682.2.
